standard.title: Circumference and Area of Circles
standard.description: solve problems involving the circumference and area of a circle using formulas and appropriate units
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand π and can calculate circumference using C = πd (from AC9M7M03). Students can calculate area of rectangles and triangles.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students derive and apply A = πr² to solve problems involving circle area and circumference, including composite shapes with circular components.

nodes.label: Deriving the area of a circle formula
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand why A = πr² using at least one informal derivation method.
nodes.minimum_width: State A = πr² and explain informally why it is reasonable (e.g. the area is between 2r² and 4r²).
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the area using a square grid or sector rearrangement method; connect the result to A = πr²; verify the formula is consistent with known approximations.
wider: Use the sector rearrangement method — divide circle into increasingly smaller sectors arranged into a near-rectangle — and show why the rectangle's dimensions give πr × r = πr².
Investigate the connection between area and circumference: A = ½ × C × r — explain this geometrically.

response_modes.reason: Students who only memorise A = πr² without any derivation experience cannot explain why the formula works or recover it when forgotten. Multiple derivation approaches build robust understanding.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who only memorise A = πr² without understanding cannot reliably choose between area and circumference formulas in Node 2 — they conflate the two formulas under pressure, particularly when asked to find radius from area (requiring rearrangement of a formula they don't understand).
success_criteria: States A = πr² and can explain the formula using at least one informal argument.
Explains why the area must be between 2r² and 4r².
Does not confuse area formula with circumference formula.

nodes.label: Applying circle area and circumference formulas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students apply A = πr² and C = 2πr to calculate area and circumference, find radius/diameter given area or circumference, and solve composite shape problems.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate area given radius; find radius given area; solve one practical problem.
nodes.typical_width: Apply both formulas in practical contexts; find any unknown (r, d, C, or A) given another; solve composite shape problems including semicircles.
wider: Explore traditional weaving designs by First Nations Australians and investigate the significance and use of circles — calculate areas and circumferences in context.
Investigate composite shapes combining circles with other polygons — e.g. area of a stadium or athletic track.

response_modes.reason: Circle measurement problems require recognising which formula applies and which quantity is unknown. Varied practical contexts build the judgment to select the right formula and direction of calculation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations weaving designs and large-scale composite shape problems (stadia, tracks) offer advancing students culturally significant and practically rich contexts for circle measurement within the Year 8 band.
success_criteria: Correctly calculates area given radius or radius given area.
Solves a composite shape problem involving circular components.
Uses an appropriate approximation for π and states it.
